sources.citation: Easton, Catherine & Diane Wroge. 2012. Manual for Alphabet Design through Community Interaction for Papua New Guinea Elementary Teacher Trainers. 2nd edition (trial ed. Sept 2002, 1st ed. Nov 2002). Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG. 40+ pp. CC BY-NC-SA.
sources.note: Only the Baimak trial alphabet (20 letters; 'q' = a 'hard b', i.e. a second bilabial stop contrast; no tone or stress symbols in the alphabet). The manual's Tone section (p. 12) exemplifies Bukawa (marks tone) and Mbñioŋko (Madang, chose not to mark tone); the Stress section (pp. 12-13) exemplifies Maia (double vowels for stress). Baimak is not mentioned in either; no statement about Baimak prosody. The absence of any stress/tone device in the Baimak trial alphabet is weak circumstantial evidence only.
